subject: POC success criteria, ownership map & escalation paths
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Recap & proposed POC plan — success criteria, owners, escalation paths

Emma — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC scheduled next week. High level: run a 3-week trial against your staging traffic to validate (1) latency and tail p99 under production-like load, (2) end-to-end correctness on 4 representative pipelines, and (3) operational handoff for your SRE/security teams.

Proposed success criteria (draft):
- Latency: average generation latency < 220ms, p95 < 380ms for 512-token requests (staging traffic).
- Throughput: sustain 80 RPS steady-state for peak window with <5% error rate.
- Quality: pass the provided eval set (FintechCo_eval_v1) with >=92% intent accuracy and no regressions on 3 priority prompts.
- Security/compliance: verification of network controls, audit logging, and encryption-in-transit at rest requirements.

Ownership (initial RACI-ish):
- Redwood infra setup (GPU pools, network routing): Alex (A), Karthik (R)
- App integration / request routing: FintechCo app team (R), Marissa (C)
- Security assessment & requirements sign-off: Grace (R), FintechCo security (C)
- Procurement & contract: FintechCo procurement (R), Alex (C)

Attachments I uploaded: fintechco_poc_requirements.docx (your onboarding inputs), redwood_poc_sow.pdf (scope & timelines), network_diagram.png (expected VPC peering). Links to HubSpot and drive folder below.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm the success criteria (above) or flag changes by Monday EOD PST.
2) Procurement handshake / PO estimate — I’ll send SOW and draft order if procurement is good to proceed.
3) Kickoff call Wednesday to walk infra checklist and assign SRE contacts.

If that works I’ll pull in the scheduling invite and a short runbook for the trial.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Emma Li <emma.li@fintechco.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@fintechco.com>, FintechCo Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & proposed POC plan — success criteria, owners, escalation paths

Alex — thanks for the clear summary. This looks good overall; a couple of clarifying items from our side: 
1) Procurement will need a line item estimate and a draft SOW with payment/term language before they can issue a PO. Procurement copied.
2) For the quality eval, can you confirm how we share the FintechCo_eval_v1 set securely? We need to keep test data in-house; can it be uploaded to the shared Drive folder with restricted access?
3) Who do we loop in for network/VPC peering on Redwood's side? Our infra lead (Daniel) will own the peering config but needs the expected CIDR/IPs and a contact.

We can confirm success criteria Monday, but please attach the SOW and the one-page pricing estimate so procurement can move.

-Emma
Emma Li
Director of Product, FintechCo

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@fintechco.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@fintechco.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & proposed POC plan — infra checklist and contacts

Emma/Daniel — looping in quick infra checklist and my contact for the peering work.

Infra notes:
- For a short 3-week trial we recommend Redwood Dedicated staging slice (shared infra) with the following: 2 x A100-equivalent instances, 80 RPS target, and prefix/KV cache enabled.
- Network: we support VPC peering and customer-managed NAT. We'll provide the peer CIDR and peer IP by kickoff.
- Data flow: all request/response traffic is TLS, and we can route audit logs to an S3 bucket or a syslog endpoint — let us know your preference.

Contacts:
- Karthik Iyer (redwood): infra lead for provisioning and peering — karthik_iyer@redwood.com, +1 (415) 555-0192
- Alex Martinez (redwood): commercial lead and procurement contact

I attached a short checklist (also in Drive). Will be on the kickoff to run the peering steps.

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Emma Li <emma.li@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & proposed POC plan — security checklist and scope

Emma/Team — a couple of security items we need to lock before kickoff: 
- Data handling: confirm whether the eval set contains any production PII. If yes, we need a DPA addendum and the dataset must be hashed or tokenized before upload.
- Audit logs: FintechCo must confirm S3 vs syslog destination. If S3, provide bucket ARN and an IAM role for write access.
- Key management: if you require customer-managed keys, we support KMS/HSM integrations — note that will add ~3 business days for setup.
- Pen test / scoping: we can provide a scoped checklist to FintechCo security; we typically avoid full pen tests in a short POC but can do targeted checks.

I'll own the security sign-off for the trial (Grace — A), and will mark Redwood security as consulted for any infra exceptions. If the dataset is clean (no PII) we can move faster.

Grace O'Connor
Head of Security | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@fintechco.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@fintechco.com>, FintechCo Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & proposed POC plan — POC owners, timeline & escalation paths (final)

Thanks all — pulling this together into a single ownership / escalation note so procurement and your infra/security teams have a clear playbook before kickoff. See condensed RACI and timeline below. I put the same doc in the Drive link.

Condensed RACI (roles marked R/A/C):
- Redwood provisioning & peering: Karthik (R), Alex (A)
- App integration & endpoint testing: FintechCo app team (R), Marissa (C)
- Security assessment & data handling: Grace (R), FintechCo security (C)
- Procurement / SOW sign-off: FintechCo procurement (R), Alex (C)
- Escalation path: 1) Daniel Park (FintechCo infra lead) -> 2) Karthik Iyer (Redwood infra) -> 3) Rishi Malhotra (Redwood Sales Eng manager)

POC timeline (target):
- Week 0 (this week): SOW sign-off + PO estimate (Procurement)
- Week 1: Redwood infra provisioning + VPC peering + smoke tests
- Week 2: Run eval traffic, collect latency/throughput metrics, iterate on batching/config
- Week 3: Final quality checks, security verification, and handoff notes; wrap & results summary

Action items (owners):
- Alex: Send SOW and 1-page pricing to procurement (today).
- Procurement (FintechCo): Provide PO or sign SOW (target Wed).
- Daniel (FintechCo): Share expected CIDR, S3 ARN (if used), and an SRE contact for kickoff.
- Grace: Provide final security checklist and DPA template if needed.

If procurement confirms, I’ll send the SOW and a calendar invite for a kickoff on Wednesday. If anything is blocking procurement sign-off, flag here and I’ll escalate to Rishi.

Attachments referenced: fintechco_poc_requirements.docx, redwood_poc_sow.pdf, network_diagram.png

Cheers,
Alex Martinez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
